area: AgentDO and agent harness: apps/server/src/agent (minus browser), core/agent/src
purpose: Run one agent per room: admit envelopes to a durable inbox, drive the pi-durable harness per human burst with mid-run rules, post bubbles exactly once, run background workers, and send model and web requests out through one invocation each.
summary: The runtime core (inbox, mid-run rules, outbox replay, workers, egress, coalesced storage) works, is mostly measured or tested, and should be frozen. The problems sit at the edges: experiment code left in the production AgentDO and in an unauthenticated experiment Worker, a 120 s in-object wait that breaks the no-setTimeout rule, and a human message that cannot interrupt a running tool.

subareas.name: inbox, envelope, text
subareas.why: Admission is idempotent by envelope id (inbox.ts:70), refuses oversize and full inboxes in one transaction, reclaims in-flight rows after 5 min, and orders human rows first. Covered by hardening.test.ts.

subareas.name: mid-run rules and drain
subareas.why: decide() is a short table: a human restarts a run only before anything visible happened and steers otherwise; non-human input is held while a human is coming. The real gap is that a running tool round is never interrupted (see problems).

subareas.name: host (crash, compaction, budget, origin)
subareas.why: Each piece answers a measured or documented need: crash-loop cap, compaction every 50 runs, budget steering, origin tracking, heartbeat. But 526 lines coordinate seven SQL flags with no single state table. The budget steer sets steered=1 before submit (host.ts:393-396), so a crash between them loses the time-up hint.

subareas.name: coalescing storage
subareas.why: Earned. docs/architecture.md:975-977 records 536 rows as shipped against 96 coalesced for one faux-model turn, on a Free plan that caps rows at 100,000 a day. It holds only single-delta partial commits, flushes before any read, and has a crash test. Real-model confirmation is still open (section 21, experiment 2).

subareas.name: workers (background child conversations)
subareas.why: Delivery is idempotent: the envelope id is work:<id>:<submission>, so a re-run of deliver() is dropped by inbox admit (inbox.ts:70). Resumes cap at 3 and concurrent workers at 3. Steer, stop and forget paths are covered by workers.test.ts.

subareas.name: outbox and split-bubbles
subareas.why: Replay is safe. A post is keyed by (run, attempt, index) and RoomDO.post dedupes on it (room/log.ts:182-190, 233-234). Reactions dedupe by current emoji (log.ts:315-322). The splitter is a small state machine for bubble pacing. blocksOf is dead.

subareas.name: egress path (AgentDO.egress, egressFetch)
subareas.why: Model requests and web_fetch go out through a self-RPC, so each request gets its own invocation and its own 50-subrequest budget. web_fetch still runs safeFetch first (web.ts:32). The RPC-budget claim cites a 2026-10-04 measurement, which is not in the repo tests.

subareas.name: AgentDO shell and experiment code
subareas.why: The production AgentDO carries a TurnExperiment, an alarm branch that checks an experiment-heartbeat row on every alarm, and three ungated experiment RPC methods. A separate Worker, measure-worker, exposes unauthenticated spin and fetch endpoints (see problems).

subareas.name: factory and effects
subareas.why: Effects are enforced: factory.ts:89 throws on any undeclared built-in tool, and every built-in tool I read is wrapped in declareEffect. Talker-only and worker-only tools sit in two opposite allowlists (factory.ts:60, work.ts:16).

subareas.name: agent tool extensions
subareas.why: Tools are plain and declare effects. ask holds the run open up to 120 s on an in-object setTimeout (messaging.ts:24, answers.ts:19). spill.ts head() is quadratic in the number of lines. builder only proposes extensions, never installs them, as the rule requires.

subareas.name: dev surface and prompt
subareas.why: Dev routes are gated by NODE_ENV and localhost (dev-route.ts:17). The fake agent gives deterministic tests with no tokens, as AGENTS.md asks. Prompt sections are ordered for cache stability.

strengths: Every inbox, outbox and worker write is keyed by a stable id, so replays after eviction converge.
A human arrival steers or restarts a run (mid-run.ts:26-33) and wakes a waiting ask (agent-do.ts:129).
receive() never waits on another Durable Object: it admits to SQL and sets an alarm (host.ts:168-173).
Model keys stay in-process: userModels takes auth per run (factory.ts:188-198).

problems.title: Unauthenticated, uncapped experiment endpoints in measure-worker
problems.evidence: apps/server/measure-worker/entry.ts:93-113: /fetch-do and /fetch-worker take n with no cap and loop fetch() to example.com; /spin-worker and /spin-do take ms with no cap. None checks a session. Line 90 routes /api/experiments/turn with no NODE_ENV gate, so any signed-in user can start real model turns there. Whether this Worker is deployed (name kiko-measure-p0-06) is UNVERIFIED.
problems.fix: Delete measure-worker once the P0-06 and section 21 numbers are recorded. Otherwise gate every route like index.ts:54-90 and cap n and ms.

problems.title: setTimeout keeps the AgentDO waiting up to 120 s, against the AGENTS.md rule
problems.evidence: core/agent/src/answers.ts:19 (setTimeout in AnswerWaiters.wait); messaging.ts:24,77 (ASK_WAIT_MS 120000). architecture.md:225 says a setTimeout keeps the object awake and blocks hibernation. This deviation is not labelled DEVIATION.
problems.fix: Label it DEVIATION in architecture.md with the cost, or return at once and let the answer arrive as a message, which messaging.ts:81-82 already does after the wait expires.

problems.title: A human message cannot interrupt a running tool round
problems.evidence: core/agent/src/mid-run.ts:33 returns steer whenever run.toolRunning. The steer joins after the round (architecture.md:194). bash runs up to 120 s (files/bash.ts:9), so the human waits that long. Only ask is interrupted early (agent-do.ts:129).
problems.fix: Decide if this is intended. If the human must always interrupt, abort the running tool on arrival, which needs a cancel contract for bash. If not, record it as a known limit.

problems.title: endRun marks the run ended last, so a crash replays its side effects
problems.evidence: room-do.ts:860-875: answerAsks, memory.trace and captureAnswer run before bubbles.markEnded (line 875), with awaits between. The outbox sets ended=1 only after endRun returns (outbox.ts:322-323), so a restart calls endRun again with first still true. Whether captureAnswer and touchChat are safe to repeat is UNVERIFIED.
problems.fix: Call markEnded before the external awaits, or key each step by runId as messageForRun does.

problems.title: spill head() is quadratic in the number of lines
problems.evidence: spill.ts:33-40 re-encodes out + line for every line. With 1-byte lines that is about 8,000 encodes of up to 8 KB, roughly 33 MB of work in one tool call.
problems.fix: Keep a running byte count and add each line's length once.

problems.title: Budget time-up hint is not atomic
problems.evidence: host.ts:393-396 sets steered=1 before root.submit. A crash between them loses the hint. The hard abort at 2x budget (host.ts:387-390) still happens.
problems.fix: Submit first, then set steered, or accept the loss because the hard abort covers it.

problems.title: Inbox render does not escape sender attributes
problems.evidence: inbox.ts:206-207 puts from.slug and from.reason into attributes without escapeXml. Slugs are validated upstream and reasons are internal, so exposure is small.
problems.fix: Pass them through escapeXml, as body and work.id already are.

overengineering.title: Measurement experiments inside the production AgentDO
overengineering.evidence: agent-do.ts:6-7,70,83-86 (TurnExperiment), 672-673 (alarm branch), 677-687 (experimentTurn, experimentStatus, experimentCoalescing, no gate). experiments/turn.ts (127 lines), count-rows.ts (31), coalescing.ts (110), measure-worker/entry.ts (about 110).
overengineering.why: Their numbers feed architecture section 21 experiment 2. Once recorded, the class, alarm branch and RPC methods have no production use, and they cause the high-severity problem. Move any needed measurement out of the agent object.

overengineering.title: Two opposite allowlists for talker and worker tools, plus split()
overengineering.evidence: factory.ts:60-62 (WORKER_ONLY, forTalker), factory.ts:99-102 (split creates a /tools sub-extension), factory.ts:118-119 (talkerOnly), work.ts:16,23 (NOT_FOR_WORKERS, forWorker).
overengineering.why: The split is earned: it fixed a measured case where the talker fetched pages itself (architecture.md:445). The duplication is one concept in two lists with opposite polarity. One per-extension flag would replace both.

overengineering.title: Dead code and a duplicate list
overengineering.evidence: factory.ts:161-163 UserExtensions.names() has no caller. outbox.ts:33 blocksOf has no caller. mid-run.ts:22,27 handle Arrival kind stop, which host.ts:524-526 arrivalOf never produces; stop uses STOP_KEY (host.ts:297-302). mid-run.test.ts:16,25-26 test only that dead branch. sandbox/src/manifest.ts:4 repeats effects.ts:3.
overengineering.why: Unused or duplicated, and removing them changes no behavior.

overengineering.title: Dev RPC methods on AgentDO
overengineering.evidence: agent-do.ts:441-444 (devInitiative) and 760-806 (devClassic, devUsage, devTrace, devBudget, devFake, devWorkers, devSeed), each behind a NODE_ENV check.
overengineering.why: About 60 lines of dev tooling sit in the production class. Moving them saves no lines but makes the class read as production code. Do it when the file is next changed.

overengineering.title: Coalesced storage wrapper
overengineering.why: Measured fix for the Free row limit (architecture.md:966-979). Each part answers a case the tests cover.

overengineering.title: Egress self-RPC and response stream copy
overengineering.why: The 50-subrequest limit per invocation binds the agent run. Abort must be applied on both sides because it cannot cross RPC.

overengineering.title: Host crash-loop, resume and compaction machinery
overengineering.why: Each mechanism fixes a failure the tests exercise: resumes, unbounded context, runs that never end.

tests: Covered: mid-run decide table (mid-run.test.ts; mid-run and team-ask verify suites); workers (workers.test.ts with workers-worker.ts: cases a to g, restart limit, fourth worker refused; workers-model suite); coalescing (coalescing-storage.test.ts: conformance, same answer, crash inside a window); answers (answers.test.ts); split-bubbles and reactions; egress (egress.test.ts, model path only); inbox (hardening.test.ts); effects (user-extensions, composio-tools, web-tools tests); factory order (agent-factory.test.ts); presence, skills, spill, recall. Gaps: no test of Outbox replay between post and the posted update; no test of RoomDO.endRun replay; no test of host.drain crashing between submit and submitted(); the RPC subrequest claim behind AgentDO.egress is untested. UNVERIFIED: real-model coalescing (architecture section 21, experiment 2).
